title: Windows installer and release payload packaging

files.role: Declares the desktop executable's non-elevated Windows compatibility and DPI/path awareness independently of installer platform gates.

blocks.title: Retain ordinary user privilege and Windows rendering declarations
blocks.explanation: asInvoker keeps the application at its caller's privilege and uiAccess=false does not request privileged accessibility access. The supportedOS identifier declares modern Windows compatibility; it is not the installer minimum-build gate. PerMonitorV2 requests per-monitor DPI behavior and longPathAware opts into supported long paths. Neither declaration proves every monitor, filesystem or screen-sharing backend is qualified. The assembly identity version is manifest metadata, distinct from the release FileVersion.

files.role: Pins the preview label, numeric Windows version, target platform and reviewed installer compiler provenance.

blocks.title: Separate human preview identity from numeric upgrade ordering
blocks.explanation: version selects0.2.0-preview.3 for filenames and release links; windowsVersion advances to0.2.0.3 for executable metadata and numeric downgrade ordering. Preview3 packages the Agency runtime-contract compatibility correction. The website test requires both release-tag links to match this version, avoiding stale targets. These values select a candidate, not proof of build/publication. win-x64, minimum Windows build22000 and reviewed Inno compiler provenance are unchanged; compiler authenticity is not an app signature.

files.role: Defines a per-user Windows11 x64 installation, guarded repair/upgrade and standard uninstall without automatic recording or forced application closure.

blocks.title: Bind installation identity, platform and lifecycle policy
blocks.explanation: PayloadDir is mandatory. Default AppVersion0.2.0-preview.3 and WindowsVersion0.2.0.3 match release.json; the builder supplies explicit overrides and the isolated fixture may override InstallerId. The numeric version advances without changing the stable production AppId or maintenance policy. lowest privilege and LocalAppData Programs keep installation per-user; x64os/build22000 remain actual platform gates. Automatic closing/restart stay disabled. Matching version literals do not prove a package or genuine old-binary upgrade was exercised.

blocks.title: Ship temporary recovery code separately from managed program files
blocks.explanation: The fresh launcher is first in the solid archive and marked dontcopy so PrepareToInstall can extract it before replacing a damaged installed launcher. The regular payload recursively installs beneath the product root. A dedicated product registry key retains the numeric version outside Inno's uninstall key, which Inno recreates during repair. InstallDelete replaces only named managed code/documentation directories; external runtime data and user saves are not targeted. Interrupted upgrades are not atomic. InstallerTest omits shortcuts. No Run section exists: Setup never launches the app, so users close it before launching without its maintenance gate.

blocks.title: Hold the installer gate and recognize an owned destination
blocks.explanation: InitializeSetup creates the named maintenance mutex for the installer lifetime. The installed launcher checks its presence before starting or revealing the app; maintenance itself is permitted. The marker must contain the exact product string after trimming. DirectoryHasFiles enumerates entries, ignores only dot entries and always closes its search handle. PrepareToInstall combines these checks before replacement. A marker is ownership bookkeeping within a same-user directory, not a cryptographic boundary against that user.

blocks.title: Reject foreign destinations and known downgrades before maintenance
blocks.explanation: An absent or empty destination is a fresh install. A nonempty destination must be marker-owned. The installed numeric version is read from its file; a missing or invalid file falls back to the product's registered numeric version. If neither works, the installer refuses rather than guessing. Packed-version comparison blocks an older installer over a known newer version. All these refusals occur before file replacement and before asking a service to stop.

blocks.title: Require bounded native maintenance before update or removal
blocks.explanation: Setup extracts the current launcher's dependencies and executes maintenance against the existing installation root, avoiding damaged old binaries during repair. A nonzero result blocks replacement with a close/stop message. Uninstall creates the same lifetime gate, then uses its installed launcher and marker; damaged files require repair first. SuppressibleMsgBox respects silent suppression instead of leaving unattended removal waiting on an invisible acknowledgment. There is no process-name kill, implicit capture cancellation or user-data purge.

files.role: Builds a new immutable output directory containing the verified speech payload, self-contained native programs, installer, portable archive and checksums.

blocks.title: Validate release inputs before staging a new runtime payload
blocks.explanation: The builder requires PowerShell7.2 and explicit compiler/output paths; the target installer requires neither PowerShell nor developer tools. Release labels are numeric preview form and win-x64. Existing output is rejected. The existing development virtual environment is preferred when Python is not supplied, and a reusable cache supports an explicit offline build. Every release invokes verify-synthetic-pcm, so imports and metadata alone cannot pass: real generated-PCM model execution must exit normally. Any bundler failure leaves a non-release partial output.

blocks.title: Publish independent native runtimes and allowlisted user documentation
blocks.explanation: App and launcher are published sequentially into separate subdirectories, avoiding conflicting dependency layouts. Both are self-contained win-x64 builds with the reviewed release/FileVersion and no debug symbols. Only the named guides, handbook PDF and installation notes are copied. ASCII marker/version files support future maintenance; no token, answer configuration or recorded transcript is copied from the developer workspace.

blocks.title: Audit hidden entries and hash the exact staged file inventory
blocks.explanation: Force enumeration includes hidden/system entries that the ZIP writer could otherwise package without review. Any reparse-point entry or private directory component is rejected. Files are also screened for known local token/settings/log names before their size and SHA256 are recorded. Git revision and dirty state describe the actual build source instead of implying an uncommitted candidate came from a clean tag. The gate supplements the bundler's allowlists; it is not a general-purpose secret scanner.

blocks.title: Keep launcher metadata small and complete inventory separate
blocks.explanation: install-manifest.json is compact metadata for the launcher's bounded reader, avoiding the earlier incompatibility where a full runtime inventory exceeded16KiB. Its own hash is then added to payload-files.json. The inventory intentionally does not hash itself; outer installer/archive hashes cover the entire artifact. Neither manifest contains personal paths, credentials or developer settings.

blocks.title: Compile unsigned assets and publish checksums only after success
blocks.explanation: The compiler receives explicit payload/version/output values and must return success with the expected Setup filename. The optional portable ZIP contains the whole audited payload, not a single executable without its dependencies. SHA256SUMS covers top-level installer/archive assets. The final message says built, not installed, signed or published to GitHub. Generated PCM did execute local models, but no audio endpoint, answer provider or installer was started.

files.role: Exercises installer replacement and removal with an isolated registry identity and destination, retaining synthetic user files and reporting bounded evidence.

blocks.title: Create a unique fixture identity and limit process ownership
blocks.explanation: A new output path and random AppId keep test uninstall registration separate from the real product. Installer processes are started explicitly and awaited for five minutes. A timeout stops only that Process object's owned process tree, including temporary installer children that otherwise outlive a wrapper; a nonexpected exit fails the fixture. This is fixture-process control, not permission to kill the user's application or speech service.

blocks.title: Install a real payload and compare bytes against the inventory
blocks.explanation: The same installer definition is compiled with a unique identity and InstallerTest, which omits production shortcuts; neither production nor fixture Setup launches the app. Silent installation uses only the fixture directory. The source file set must exactly match inventory entries plus the inventory itself; each installed inventoried file must match size and SHA256. The actual native launcher then validates the bounded compact manifest, and maintenance tests the idle/no-owned-service path without starting default application behavior.

blocks.title: Exercise repair, downgrade protection, removal and foreign-folder refusal
blocks.explanation: Same-version reinstall must restore the version and retain an external synthetic note. The fixture then removes the installed launcher and corrupts its version file to exercise recovery from fresh installer code and registry metadata. Upgrade uses a simulated older version record, not an actual old-binary compatibility matrix. A newer record must produce exit7 without replacement. Uninstall must remove application/registration while retaining the external note; a nonempty unrecognized destination must also refuse without erasing its sentinel.

blocks.title: Clean only the fixture installation and emit a scoped receipt
blocks.explanation: Finally restores the deliberately renamed launcher and numeric version before invoking the fixture's remaining uninstaller, so a failed damaged-install case cannot deadlock cleanup on its own injected damage. Cleanup failures surface. The successful receipt records each Boolean, payload count and no-audio/no-model-request boundary. It excludes clean-VM, shortcut and actual historical-binary qualification and records that production Setup has no automatic launch.
